author: Temminck & Schlegel, 1848
habitat: 섬과 바닷가의 덤불숲, 숲 가장자리, 관목이 우거진 풀밭

months.note: 주로 4월 초~5월 하순에 남해와 서해의 섬을 지나가며, 가을에는 드물게 기록된다.

summary: 우리나라에서는 봄과 가을에 서남해안을 거쳐 가는 나그네새이다. 곤충과 씨앗을 즐겨 먹는다. 지나친 살충제 사용과 불법 포획이 이 새를 위협하고 있다.

points.ko: 잿빛 녹색이나 갈색 띤 녹색 등

points.en: black shaft streaks on the back

sexes.male: 머리와 윗면이 회녹색이고 눈앞과 턱이 검으며, 멱과 아랫면이 노랗고 눈 둘레에 가는 흰 테가 뚜렷하다.
sexes.female: 수컷과 비슷하나 색이 더 수수하고 갈색을 띠며, 눈앞과 턱이 검지 않다.

young: 첫겨울 어린새는 암컷과 비슷해 눈앞과 턱이 검지 않고, 윗면이 더 올리브 갈색이며 등과 셋째날개깃의 붉은 갈색 깃 가장자리가 넓다.

similar.how: 무당새는 눈 둘레에 가는 흰 테가 뚜렷하고 멱과 가슴에 줄무늬가 없지만, 섬촉새는 흰 눈테가 없고 암컷과 어린새는 가슴에 갈색 줄무늬가 있다.

art.subject: Yellow Bunting (Emberiza sulphurata), adult male on spring passage (April–May): head olive-green with a yellowish tinge; blackish lores; a distinct, complete, narrow white eye-ring; chin and throat yellow; breast and belly yellow, the breast sides and flanks washed olive with fine dark streaks on the flanks; lower belly and undertail coverts whitish; mantle and back greyish olive-brown with black shaft streaks; wings brown with two whitish wing bars and rufous-buff edges to the tertials; rump greyish-olive; tail dark with white outer feathers; bill grey; dark eye; pink legs.
art.pose: perched in a low shrub, side view
art.scene: Korean southwestern island woodland edge with low shrubs and grassy clearings during spring migration in late April–May; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male spring, side view perched in a low shrub: olive-green head, blackish lores, narrow complete white eye-ring, yellow throat, breast and belly with fine dark flank streaks, greyish olive-brown back with black shaft streaks, two whitish wing bars, grey bill, pink legs
adult male, three-quarter view from behind: greyish-green to brownish-green mantle and back with neat black shaft streaks, whitish wing bars, white outer tail feathers
art.build: Small bunting, about the size of a sparrow but neater and slimmer, with a rounded head without a crest and a medium-length tail with white outer feathers. Bill small, conical and pointed, shorter than the head. Legs pinkish. Quiet and unobtrusive, feeding on the ground under shrubs and perching low in bushes.
avoid: Do not paint a dark grey hood with a blackish face and no eye-ring — that is Black-faced Bunting (Emberiza spodocephala).
Do not paint a crest, a black mask or a bright yellow supercilium (Yellow-throated Bunting traits).
Do not paint chestnut anywhere in the plumage.
Do not omit the white eye-ring; it is the most obvious mark on the face.
